Front B closes as PREMISE REFUTED. It was commissioned on the hypothesis that
the fixed-in-timesteps `distance` filter was cutting the mature phase short on
20160735 and 20203947, with a view to letting `length_scale` govern it. The
read-only diagnosis (commit 7fbda56) refuted that: under the reference config
`distance` removes ZERO extrema across all 47 training series.

REMOVAL

`distance` is gone from get_periods, determine_periods, find_peaks_valleys and
_refine_extrema, and from the calibration app and its layer inspector.
`prominence` and `prominence_relative` are untouched.

It belongs in the inert-parameter record for a reason the others there do not
share: it is not inert because a mode switch disables it. The mechanism is
live — push the value high enough and extrema disappear and phases change. It
is inert because `prominence_relative` has already done the work by the time
it runs. Redundancy, not absence of mechanism, which is why a UI guard could
not express it and the parameter was removed instead. Swept over the 47
training series at prominence_relative=0.30: 0 extrema removed at every value
up to 14, one inert extremum at 15-18, first phase change at 20 — against a
calibrated value of 5. The binding quantity is the smallest same-type gap
among post-prominence survivors, 14, on 20170760.

(969904b) and never shipped in a release. Passing it now raises the ordinary
Python TypeError.

mature_method="amplitude" it stops scaling the mature window, but it still
scales the intensification and decay thresholds — measured to change the phase
output on 20160735, 20191014 and 20203947. It therefore carries a scoped note
naming which role is inactive and which stays live, instead of the blanket
`disabled=True` that Min. mature length / Mature distance carry. Disabling it
would present a live, outcome-changing control as inert. Divergence from the
brief raised and accepted by Danilo.

commit.body:
Three problems from the real-Chromium run of tests/test_label_browser.py,
investigated in the requested order before any fix was applied.

PROBLEM 1 — drag grabbed the wrong boundary (max priority)

The three-curve-overlay hypothesis was WRONG: reproduced with zero overlays
active, and confirmed against unmodified develop-v2.1 in a throwaway
worktree (same steps, same result) — this predates every commit on this
front. Real cause: _CHART_JS attached one pointerdown listener per boundary's
grip/edge hit-rect, keyed to that boundary's own `k` via closure. Adjacent
boundaries' hit-rects legitimately overlap whenever their combined tolerance
reach exceeds their spacing (the bar's width IS the tolerance -- real data,
not something to shrink), and whichever rect was appended LAST always won
the overlap by DOM z-order, silently grabbing the wrong boundary. Two
boundaries 4 steps apart with margin 5 each -- an entirely ordinary label --
overlap this way.

Fix: one pointerdown listener on the whole chart; a `pickTarget(x)` function
picks the boundary by DISTANCE to its own geometry (edge targets checked
before body targets, preserving the original z-order's intent), never by
which element the browser painted on top. setStart/setTol/onMove/onKey/at
are untouched -- they only ever read clientX and step index, never a curve
value, so nothing about the fix touches them.

Fixing the picking bug alone was not sufficient: several hardcoded drag
targets (`drag_boundary(2, 61)`, `drag_boundary(1, 40)`) assumed neighbour
boundaries had more room than the currently-loaded real case (now 63/63
labelled, so always the same case) actually leaves -- correctly clamped
against a neighbour, not a bug, just a `fresh` fixture that pinned rows 1-2
but not row 3, and one standalone test that never pinned row 2 at all. Both
completed to control every row they depend on.

Added test_dragging_never_changes_the_number_of_phases: pins n_rows() before
and after a drag, a tolerance-edge drag, an arrow-key nudge, and a release-
outside-the-svg drag -- length alone would not have caught the original bug
(same length, wrong entry moved), so this checks it explicitly, as asked.

PROBLEM 2 — tests desynced from the app, one justified, one not

poke_sidebar() timeout: Streamlit's slider moved to a react-aria
implementation exposing a visually-hidden `<input type="range">` under
`role="group"`, not a `role="slider"` element the old selector matched.
Nothing on this front touches the filter sidebar -- confirmed by inspecting
the live DOM. Retargeted to `input[type="range"]`.

phase_name()'s IndexError: NOT the case-navigation dropdown's index shift --
confirmed by reproducing the SAME IndexError on unmodified develop-v2.1.
Streamlit's selectbox is also now a react-aria combobox whose chosen value
lives in an `<input value="...">` attribute, not as rendered text; `.inner_
text()` returns '' for every selectbox regardless of position, which is what
`.splitlines()[0]` was raising on. Rewritten to read via `get_by_label(...)
.input_value()` -- correct AND position-independent, so it no longer cares
how many selectboxes precede it.

PROBLEM 3 — 1440x800 overflow

RESERVE (the chart's height budget subtracted from window height) hadn't
grown to match new content between the chart and the button row (the
"Cannot save yet" caption, present by default since the tab opens in
Inspection; the overwrite-confirmation checkbox, present for any
already-labelled case). 400 -> 420 (410 closed the span but missed that the
chart's own 10px scrollMarginTop pushes its absolute bottom position past
the window height too). Remeasured with the real working_area() helper at
all three sizes: 1440x800 now fits with margin, 1680x950/1920x1080 chart
heights unchanged (already at the `data.h` cap there, not shrunk).

commit.body:
Two corrections to the previous commit on this branch:

1. Per-phase uncertainty was only half-built: storage already had one value
   per boundary (open_unsure/close_unsure for the two series edges, unsure
   per phase for the internal ones), but the table only exposed a single
   "not sure" checkbox per row (that row's own START). Every row now shows
   BOTH its start and end edge. Row k's "end unsure" and row k+1's "start
   unsure" are two different Streamlit widgets pointed at the identical
   stored boundary; label_tab.py's _phase_table reads both raw results after
   the loop and reconciles them against the old value (whichever disagrees
   is the one just clicked), then bumps `rev` so both widgets redraw from
   the single new value on the next rerun -- they cannot show different
   states for more than that one rerun. Row 0's start is now enabled
   (open_unsure, previously hardcoded False+disabled); the last row's end is
   close_unsure. No storage change from the prior commit.

2. The three process_vorticity layers (filtered_vorticity, vorticity_smoothed,
   vorticity_smoothed2) now draw in the SAME interactive chart as the raw
   series and the boundary bars, not a separate st.line_chart preview.
   Assessed the custom drag component first, per instructions to stop and
   report if it needed a large rewrite: it did not, because the pointer/
   keyboard handlers already read only `clientX` and the step index, never a
   curve value, so the drag/select/keyboard code is untouched by this diff
   (verified: zero lines changed in setStart/setTol/onDown/onMove/onKey/at).
   What changed is confined to _CHART_JS's build step: one shared y-domain
   computed from the raw series plus every ACTIVE overlay (no per-curve
   normalisation -- a flat overlay stays visibly flat), one <path> per active
   layer drawn after the raw path (raw stays visually behind, thickest,
   darkest), an in-chart legend naming each layer, and the reuse-before-
   rebuild guard extended to key on the active overlay set too (toggling a
   layer changes which <path> elements must exist, which the lightweight
   `update()` reposition pass does not touch, so it now forces a rebuild the
   same way a changed phase count already did). chart_payload()'s own pinned
   return keys are untouched -- the overlay list is merged into the wire
   payload by _draw(), one level up, so the raw-series-only contract the
   blindness tests check stays exactly what it was.
   app.py's _label_overlays() now returns {name: {label, color, values}};
   label_tab.py still imports nothing from cyclophaser (unchanged AST guard).

Tests: tests/test_label_apptest.py is new -- Streamlit AppTest (no browser)
coverage for the two Python-side risks that don't need a real pointer: the
start/end-unsure reconciliation in both directions, and that switching
overlay layers on/off never moves a phase. tests/test_label_browser.py gets
the equivalent real-browser versions (the outdated
test_the_first_row_cannot_be_unsure is replaced -- row 0's start is
deliberately enabled now) plus the specific drag-with-overlays-on check
requested; these require Playwright+Chromium, absent in this environment, so
they are UNVERIFIED here -- run before merge.
